1.1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by God our Savior and the Lord Jesus Christ, our hope,
1.2: To Timothy, my true son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.
1.3: As I told you when I went to Macedonia, stay in Ephesus and tell some folks not to teach anything other than the real gospel,
1.4: Don't get caught up in stories and endless family trees that just lead to arguments instead of building up in faith.
1.5: The point of all this teaching is love, coming from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith.
1.6: But some people got distracted and turned to empty talk,
1.7: They wanna be teachers of the law, but don't even understand what they're saying or what they're trying to push.
1.8: But we know that the law is good if you use it right,
1.9: The law isn't for the righteous person, it's for the lawless and rebellious, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for those who kill their fathers and mothers, for murderers,
1.10: For people out here living in sin, for those messing with others' lives, for liars, for those making false oaths, and anything else that's against sound teaching—
1.11: According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which I've been trusted with.
1.12: And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who gave me strength, because He saw me as faithful and put me in the ministry,
1.13: Even though I was once a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an arrogant person, but I got mercy 'cause I didn't know what I was doing, I was just out here in unbelief.
1.14: The grace of our Lord was so much more than enough, along with faith and love, which are in Christ Jesus.
1.15: Here's a true saying that's worthy of everyone accepting: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, and I'm the worst of them.
1.16: But I got mercy, so that Jesus Christ could show His patience in me, as an example for those who will believe in Him and get eternal life.
1.17: Now to the eternal, immortal, invisible King, to God who's the only wise one, be all the honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
1.18: This charge I give you, son Timothy, based on the prophecies spoken over you, so that you can fight the good fight,
1.19: Hold on to faith and a good conscience, which some have rejected, and because of that, their faith has crashed like a shipwreck,
1.20: Like Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan so they could learn not to disrespect God.

2.1: So first off, I'm telling y'all to pray for everybody—supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving for all people,
2.2: For kings and all those in authority, so we can live a peaceful, quiet life, full of godliness and respect.
2.3: This is good and pleases God, our Savior,
2.4: Who wants everyone to be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth.
2.5: There's only one God, and one Mediator between God and mankind—the Man, Christ Jesus,
2.6: Who gave Himself as a ransom for all, to be shown at the right time.
2.7: That's why I was chosen to be a preacher and apostle—I'm speaking the truth in Christ, no cap—a teacher to the Gentiles in faith and truth.
2.8: I want the men to pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands, without anger or doubting.
2.9: And for the women, I need you to keep it modest—dress appropriately, no need to overdo it with the flashy clothes, expensive jewelry, or braided hair.
2.10: It's about looking like someone who's living out godliness, not someone flexing their appearance. What really matters is the good works that show what's in your heart.
2.11: Let women learn quietly, with full submission—no rush, just take your time and listen,
2.12: And I'm not letting a woman teach or have authority over a man—she should be quiet and not try to take control.
2.13: Adam was made first, then Eve.
2.14: Adam wasn't deceived, but the woman got tricked and fell into sin.
2.15: But don't get it twisted—women will still be saved through childbearing, if they keep living in faith, love, and holiness, with self-control.

3.1: This is a real one: If a man wants to be a bishop (a leader in the church), he's desiring a good job.
3.2: A bishop gotta be blameless, the husband of one wife, temperate, sober-minded, good behavior, hospitable, and able to teach.
3.3: Not out here drunk all the time, not violent, not out here chasing money, but gentle, not starting fights, and not greedy for stuff.
3.4: He gotta know how to run his house right, keeping his kids in line with respect and honor.
3.5: 'Cause if a man can't handle his own house, how's he gonna take care of God's church?
3.6: Don't make him a newbie, cause if he's too full of pride, he'll fall into the same trap the devil did.
3.7: He also needs a good reputation outside the church, or he might end up in disgrace and fall into the devil's trap.
3.8: Deacons gotta be respectful, not two-faced, not always drinking, and not chasing money.
3.9: They gotta hold the faith with a pure conscience.
3.10: Let them be tested first, and then let them serve as deacons if they're found blameless.
3.11: Their wives need to be respectful too, no gossiping, self-controlled, and faithful in everything.
3.12: Deacons gotta be the husbands of one wife, running their households and kids well.
3.13: When deacons serve well, they get a good name and boldness in the faith of Jesus Christ.
3.14: I'm writing this to you 'cause I hope to come to you soon,
3.15: But if I get delayed, I want you to know how to behave in God's house, which is the church of the living God—the pillar and foundation of the truth.
3.16: And here's the mystery that's without controversy: God was revealed in the flesh, Justified in the Spirit, Seen by angels, Preached among the Gentiles, Believed on in the world, Received up in glory.

4.1: Now, the Spirit's straight up telling us that in the last days, some folks are gonna fall away from the faith, listening to deceiving spirits and doctrines of demons,
4.2: They gon' be out here lying and pretending, with their conscience burned like it's been touched with a hot iron,
4.3: They gon' be out here saying stuff like don't marry and don't eat certain foods, even though God created those foods to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
4.4: Everything God made is good, and ain't nothing to be turned down if it's received with thanks,
4.5: It's set apart as holy by God's word and prayer.
4.6: If you teach these things to the brothers and sisters, you're gonna be a good servant of Jesus Christ, fed with the words of faith and good teaching that you've been following closely.
4.7: But stay away from nonsense and old stories that don't build you up—train yourself in godliness.
4.8: Physical exercise might help a little, but godliness is good for everything, with promise of a good life here and the one to come.
4.9: This is a true saying, and it's worth accepting.
4.10: We work hard for this, and we get ridiculed for it, but we trust in the living God, who's the Savior of all people, especially those who believe.
4.11: These are the things you need to teach and command.
4.12: Don't let anyone look down on you because you're young, but be an example to the believers in word, in conduct, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
4.13: Until I get there, keep giving attention to reading, encouraging people, and teaching the doctrine.
4.14: Don't neglect the gift that's inside of you, the one given to you through prophecy and the laying on of hands by the elders.
4.15: Think on these things; throw yourself fully into them, so that everyone can see how much you're growing.
4.16: Watch yourself and the teaching—stay committed to both, 'cause by doing this, you'll save yourself and everyone who hears you.

5.1: Don't go rebuking an older man, but encourage him like he's your father, younger men like your brothers,
5.2: Older women like your mothers, and younger women like your sisters—with all purity.
5.3: Honor widows who are really widows.
5.4: But if a widow has kids or grandkids, let them step up first, learn to show respect at home, and take care of their parents. That's good and what God wants.
5.5: The real widow, the one left alone, trusts in God and stays praying and supplicating, day and night.
5.6: But the one out here living for pleasure is spiritually dead while she's still living.
5.7: Teach these things so that they can be blameless.
5.8: But if anyone doesn't take care of their own family—especially their household—they've denied the faith and are worse than an unbeliever.
5.9: Don't let a widow under sixty years old be added to the list, unless she's been the wife of one man,
5.10: And has a good reputation for good works: if she raised children, showed hospitality to strangers, washed the saints' feet, helped the afflicted, and followed every good work.
5.11: But don't take in younger widows, 'cause when they start getting restless, they wanna remarry,
5.12: And that brings condemnation 'cause they left their first faith.
5.13: They get lazy, hopping from house to house, and not just idle but gossips and busybodies, saying stuff they shouldn't.
5.14: So, I want the younger widows to marry, have children, manage their homes, and not give the devil a chance to speak against them.
5.15: Some have already turned away after Satan.
5.16: If any believing man or woman has widows in their family, they should take care of them so the church isn't burdened. The church should only care for true widows.
5.17: Elders who do their job well should be worthy of double honor, especially those working hard in the Word and doctrine.
5.18: The Scripture says: "Don't muzzle an ox while it's working the grain," and "The laborer is worthy of their wages."
5.19: Don't accept an accusation against an elder unless it's confirmed by two or three witnesses.
5.20: If they're sinning, rebuke them in front of everyone, so others will learn to take it seriously.
5.21: I charge you before God, Jesus Christ, and the elect angels to observe these rules without bias or partiality.
5.22: Don't be quick to lay hands on anyone or get involved in other people's sins. Keep yourself pure.
5.23: Don't just drink water—use a little wine for your stomach and your frequent health problems.
5.24: Some people's sins are obvious and they're dealt with before judgment, but others show up later.
5.25: Likewise, some good works are clearly visible, but others can't be hidden.

6.1: All the bondservants under the yoke, let them respect their masters and give them honor, so that God's name and His message don't get disrespected.
6.2: And if your master is a believer, don't look down on them just 'cause they're your brother or sister in Christ. Serve them with even more love, 'cause they're also in the family of believers. Teach these things and keep encouraging people to live right.
6.3: If anyone's teaching something different and isn't sticking to the true gospel—the words of Jesus and the doctrine that leads to godliness,
6.4: They're just full of pride, knowin' nothing, and caught up in arguments and debates, which only lead to envy, strife, insults, and evil suspicions.
6.5: It's just a bunch of useless drama from people with corrupt minds, who don't have the truth. They think godliness is a way to make money, so stay away from them.
6.6: But godliness with contentment? That's true wealth.
6.7: We came into this world with nothing, and we ain't takin' nothing out of it either.
6.8: If we got food and clothes, we should be good and be content.
6.9: But those who're chasing after riches, they fall into temptation and traps, and it leads to a bunch of foolish and dangerous desires that drag people down into destruction.
6.10: The love of money is the root of all kinds of evil—some people have even strayed from the faith because of their greed, and they've hurt themselves with all kinds of pain.
6.11: But you, man of God, run from all that mess. Instead, chase after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, and gentleness.
6.12: Fight the good fight of faith. Lay hold of eternal life, to which you were called and have already confessed in front of many witnesses.
6.13: I urge you in front of God, who gives life to all things, and before Jesus Christ, who confessed the good confession before Pilate,
6.14: Keep this commandment clean and pure until the Lord Jesus comes back,
6.15: He's the one who's gonna be revealed at the right time, the blessed and only King, the King of kings, the Lord of lords,
6.16: Who alone has immortality, living in light no one can touch, whom nobody has seen or can see. To Him be the honor and power forever. Amen.
6.17: Tell those who are rich in this world not to be stuck up or trust in uncertain riches, but in God, who gives us everything to enjoy.
6.18: Let them do good, let them be rich in good works, always ready to give, always willing to share,
6.19: Storing up a solid foundation for the future, so they can lay hold of eternal life.
6.20: Timothy, guard what's been trusted to you. Don't get caught up in all the empty talk and nonsense that's falsely called knowledge—
6.21: Some folks have wandered away from the faith 'cause they got caught up in that mess. Grace be with you. Amen.
